$comment: Performance budgets for the shipped JS bundle — TDD Part 5 §10.1 (performance gate,
release-blocking) and Part 1 §8 NFR-01 (cold start → first meaningful frame < 1 s).
Enforced per PR by scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs, wired into ci.yml's Bundle gate.
WHAT THIS MEASURES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. This is the size of the Hermes bytecode Metro
produces — the artifact a device must download, parse and execute before the first frame.
It is the largest single lever engineering controls on NFR-01. It is NOT a latency
measurement: PDD's per-screen budgets (Today cached render < 500 ms, checklist ack
< 100 ms) are user-perceived timings on real hardware, and a GitHub-hosted emulator
cannot measure them honestly. Those remain open — see docs/devops/GO_NO_GO.md §7.1.
WHY A CEILING AND NOT A RATCHET. The bundle is NOT byte-reproducible: two exports of the
same commit measured 5279878 vs 5279857 (android) and 5286013 vs 5286045 (ios) — tens of
bytes of jitter. A zero-tolerance ratchet would therefore fail at random. A ceiling with
real headroom is unaffected by ~32 bytes and still catches what matters.
HOW THE NUMBER WAS CHOSEN. Measured 2026-08-08 at 5.04 MiB (both platforms; 5,286,045 and
5,279,878 bytes). The budget is 6 MiB = 6,291,456 bytes — about 19% headroom. Wide enough
that ordinary feature work does not trip it, narrow enough that one heavy dependency
(typically 100 KB–1 MB) does.
⚠️ UNITS ARE MiB THROUGHOUT, AND EXPO DISAGREES. `expo export` prints decimal MB (it reports
this same bundle as 5.29 MB) while this file and the checker use binary MiB. Mixing the two
is how the headroom here was first written as 13% instead of 19%. All values are bytes; the
MiB labels are presentation only.
RAISING THIS NUMBER IS THE POINT, NOT A NUISANCE. The gate exists to make bundle growth a
decision someone makes on purpose, in a reviewed diff, rather than something that happens.
If a change genuinely needs the room, raise it here and say why in the PR.
